title: Armed Shoplifter Rushes Officer During Escape
description:

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

Walmart surveillance footage shows the suspect attempting to run out of the store as he's being pursued by police. As he gets to the door, the officer waiting there stops him in his tracks, and the Good Samaritan begins to help immediately, along with the officer who was pursuing close behind him. The large knife can be seen falling out of the suspect's backpack due to the struggle, and the interaction continues as seen in the body cam footage. The suspect was charged with retail theft, disorderly conduct, resisting an officer, carrying a concealed knife, habitual criminality, and felony resisting an officer causing injury. He is innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. There's something you never forget in patrol, and that's when a simple call explodes into something you barely can control. Now, a shoplifter on the run doesn't sound like much, right? Until suddenly you've got multiple cops, a suspect who won't quit, and even an older man who gets tangled in the fight. The officer's tunnel vision locks him to the runner, but so does everyone else's curiosity. Now, the taser deployment in this situation does force us to ask some hard questions. About how many times can an officer pull the trigger before it stops being effective and starts looking excessive to the public? And if a suspect fights through shock after shock doesn't mean that the taser failed or doesn't mean his body is so amped up on adrenaline or drugs that he's beyond normal control. But for me, this is the hardest one. I'd be bound to need to stop the struggle right now, with the risk of inflicting serious harm by sending electricity through a man's body again and again. And training drills always show the clean version, quick takedown, cuffs on, suspect's secured. But when reality hits, why does it always feel like a Brazilian jiu-jitsu match in the middle of the street? because it's rarely neat and polished when arresting people. And I've been there also. You're hanging on to one arm, your partner's got the other, and suddenly someone from left field decides to grab them like they're part of the team. Now, the bravery is commendable, but always remember, you can truly get hurt getting involved. My question is, when you see even the elderly getting involved, what type of strain are the people sworn to hold the line truly under?
